Ghost cache-poisoning via unauthenticated x-ghost-preview header (CVE-2026-53943) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests carrying the `x-ghost-preview` header hitting a Ghost frontend behind a shared cache (Fastly/Cloudflare/nginx proxy_cache). An unauthenticated attacker uses this header to alter the rendered response, which the shared cache then stores and serves to other visitors — enabling reflected/stored XSS and, on same-domain admin deployments, staff-account takeover. Rationale: The `x-ghost-preview` request header is the exact, article-named injection vector for CVE-2026-53943 and is not a benign header any normal browser or bot emits — its presence in inbound edge/WAF logs is a near-zero-FP signal. Splunk uses TERM() to match the header token in raw web events (headers are not first-class CIM Web fields); Sentinel searches the CEF Message/RequestContext where WAFs surface matched request headers. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-62q6-4hv4-vjrw • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-53943
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ghost's own preview/staging workflow where an authenticated editor legitimately requests preview content (the header is used as designed) — distinguishable by an accompanying valid admin session cookie/authenticated source IP
  • Security-scanning tools (Burp, Nuclei, internal DAST) firing the CVE-2026-53943 test payload during an authorized assessment
  • Synthetic-monitoring or QA scripts that replay saved requests including custom headers
  • A misconfigured internal proxy that unconditionally forwards/injects a preview header on all upstream requests
Suppression filter
| where not (RequestClientApplication has_any ("Burp","Nuclei","HealthCheck","pingdom","StatusCake") or SourceIP in ("127.0.0.1"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the target host runs Ghost <= v6.36.0 and whether frontend and admin share the same domain (same-domain = staff-takeover exposure). Check whether the shared cache stored the response (look for a subsequent cache-HIT on the same URL/varied output) and identify the source IP + user-agent. 2) CONTAIN: At the caching layer, add a rule to bypass/deny cache for any request bearing `x-ghost-preview`; purge the affected cache keys/URLs. Upgrade Ghost to v6.37.0+. If same-domain admin and poisoning is confirmed, use Settings > Danger Zone > 'Reset all authentication' (Ghost v6.41.0+) to invalidate staff sessions. 3) HUNT: Pivot on the source IP for other header-injection or preview-abuse attempts; review admin/staff sign-ins and session activity after the poisoning window for signs of account takeover; check edge logs for other cached poisoned URLs served to third parties.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DeviceVendor in~ ("Fastly","Cloudflare","NGINX","Imperva","F5","Akamai") or DeviceProduct has_any ("WAF","proxy","cache")
| where Message has "x-ghost-preview" or RequestContext has "x-ghost-preview"
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fleet valuesFrom cross-namespace secret/configmap reference (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts Rancher Fleet GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle custom resources whose spec contains a `valuesFrom` block with a secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef, the exact mechanism CVE-2026-44935 abuses to read secrets in namespaces the tenant is not authorized for. Article-specific because it pivots on the Fleet CRD resource names plus the `valuesFrom` key-reference structure rather than generic secret access. Rationale: Uses the exact Fleet CRD resource names (gitrepos/helmops/bundles from go:github.com/rancher/fleet) and the `valuesFrom` + secretKeyRef/configMapKeyRef structure named in GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x as the exploitation vector; high-fidelity because legitimate fleet.yaml normally references secrets in the same namespace only. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-namespace GitOps deployment where an operator intentionally references a shared config namespace
  • Fleet platform team testing valuesFrom against a sanctioned central secrets namespace
  • CI pipelines that template Bundles with valuesFrom to a common values ConfigMap
  • Upgrade migrations that recreate existing GitRepo resources with unchanged valuesFrom blocks
Suppression filter
| where not (Username has "system:serviceaccount:cattle-fleet-system" and ObjNamespace == extract(@"namespace:\s*([a-z0-9-]+)", 1, ReqStr))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full RequestObject; compare the namespace inside valuesFrom to ObjectRef.namespace and to the tenant that owns the requesting Username — a mismatch to a namespace the tenant has no RBAC in is the true positive. 2) Contain: delete/suspend the offending GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle, and rotate any secret whose name/namespace/key appears in the valuesFrom reference (advisory explicitly recommends rotation). 3) Hunt: enumerate all Fleet CRs created by the same Username across the cluster and check whether the Fleet agent service account subsequently read those referenced secrets (see companion fan-out UC).
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend ObjResource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), ObjNamespace = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)
| where ObjResource in ("gitrepos","helmops","bundles")
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where ReqStr has "valuesFrom" and (ReqStr has "secretKeyRef" or ReqStr has "configMapKeyRef")
| where ReqStr has "namespace"    // cross-namespace ref requires an explicit namespace inside valuesFrom
| project TimeGenerated, Username, Verb, ObjResource, ObjNamespace, RequestUri, ReqStr
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fleet agent service account reads secrets across multiple namespaces (CVE-2026-44935) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the downstream-cluster fingerprint of CVE-2026-44935: the Fleet agent service account issuing get/list of secrets or configmaps across an abnormal number of distinct namespaces within a short window, indicating cross-tenant credential harvesting via unrestricted valuesFrom/HelmOp deployment. Article-specific because it keys on the Fleet agent SA identity and the cross-namespace fan-out the advisory tells defenders to review logs for. Rationale: Pivots on the Fleet agent service account identity (cattle-fleet-system fleet-agent) reading secrets/configmaps across namespaces — the exact post-exploit behaviour GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x tells operators to review cluster logs for and to drive credential rotation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xr65-5cpm-g36x • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/007/
ATT&CKT1552.007 T1613
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate multi-tenant cluster where the Fleet agent SA is authorized to deploy into many namespaces by design
  • Initial Fleet onboarding/bootstrap that syncs bundles into a large set of namespaces at once
  • Backup/DR tooling running under a fleet-labelled SA enumerating secrets
  • Cluster-wide chart rollout (e.g. cert-manager, monitoring) driven through Fleet touching every namespace
Response runbook
1) Triage: list the distinct namespaces and secret names the Fleet agent SA touched; confirm against the tenant boundary — reads into namespaces owned by a different tenant are the true positive. 2) Contain: rotate the Fleet agent service account token and every secret it read cross-tenant, then apply the patched-version Policy resource pinning a least-privilege service account per GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle namespace. 3) Hunt: correlate back to companion UC (valuesFrom cross-namespace references) to identify which GitRepo/HelmOp/Bundle CR triggered the reads and which tenant Username authored it; upgrade Fleet to v0.15.2/v0.14.6/0.13.11/v0.12.15.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where Verb in ("get","list","watch")
| extend Resource = tostring(ObjectRef.resource), NS = tostring(ObjectRef.namespace)
| where Resource in ("secrets","configmaps")
| where Username has "serviceaccount" and Username has "fleet"
| summarize NamespaceCount = dcount(NS), Namespaces = make_set(NS, 50), Requests = count() by Username, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where NamespaceCount > 3    // 3 = a single Fleet agent normally serves a bounded tenant namespace set; fan-out beyond that is the CVE signal
| order by NamespaceCount desc

Rancher CVE-2026-44939 exploit URL: authImage YAML injection in /v3/import cluster-import request AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to the Rancher cluster-import endpoint /v3/import/{token}_{clusterId}.yaml where the authImage query parameter carries URL-encoded newlines or injected YAML keys (command/hostNetwork/securityContext). A well-formed import only ever passes an OCI image reference here, so encoded CR/LF or YAML keywords in authImage are the exploit signature for CVE-2026-44939. Rationale: authImage is documented to accept only an OCI image reference; the presence of %0a/%0d/%250a or YAML keywords (command/hostNetwork/securityContext) inside it on the /v3/import path is the exact CVE-2026-44939 break-out. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory, GitLab Advisory DB and Tenable. Defender left empty: Defender XDR does not ingest web-server access logs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mhc6-2gfq-xx62 • https://advisories.gitlab.com/golang/github.com/rancher/rancher/CVE-2026-44939/ • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-44939
ATT&CKT1190 T1610
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate cluster registration where authImage carries a normal image ref (no encoded newline/YAML keyword) — excluded by the injection-marker clause
  • DAST/vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Nuclei) probing the endpoint with CVE-2026-44939 test payloads
  • Authorized red-team / pentest validating the patch
  • A benign query string that happens to contain the substring 'command' outside authImage (rare on this path)
Response runbook
1) Triage: URL-decode the full authImage value and confirm it contains a newline followed by a YAML key (command:/args:/hostNetwork:). Identify source IP, whether the request returned 200, and which token_clusterId was targeted. 2) Contain: treat the referenced cluster registration token as burned — rotate it and the cattle service-account credentials; block the source IP at the proxy; confirm Rancher is on a patched build (v2.14.2/2.13.6/2.12.10/2.11.14/2.10.12). 3) Hunt: pivot to the downstream cluster's audit log for a kube-api-auth DaemonSet create/modify in cattle-system (UC3) and to endpoints for the matching kubectl apply (UC2).

| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url contains "/v3/import/" and Url contains "authImage"
| where Url contains "%0a" or Url contains "%0d" or Url contains "%250a" or Url contains "command" or Url contains "hostNetwork" or Url contains "securityContext"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, HttpMethod, Url, UserAgent = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpStatusCode
| order by TimeGenerated desc

kubectl apply of malicious Rancher import URL (authImage newline injection) on endpoint AIDelivery High
Hunts kubectl apply invocations pointed at a remote Rancher import manifest whose URL carries the CVE-2026-44939 authImage payload (URL-encoded newlines / injected YAML). This is the victim-operator execution step the advisory describes — applying a maliciously crafted /v3/import URL. Rationale: Ties the article's 'operator runs kubectl apply against a maliciously crafted URL' step to a concrete process event: kubectl + apply + /v3/import/ + authImage. Requiring authImage plus an injection marker keeps this near-zero FP. CloudWatch left empty — endpoint process telemetry, not CloudTrail. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mhc6-2gfq-xx62 • https://www.tenable.com/cve/CVE-2026-44939
ATT&CKT1204.001 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Operator applying a legitimate import manifest (authImage is a plain image ref, no %0a/command) — excluded by injection markers

  • A security engineer reproducing the CVE in a lab
  • Shell history replay or documentation copy-paste that includes an encoded URL
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine contains "authImage" and (ProcessCommandLine contains "%0a" or ProcessCommandLine contains "%0d" or ProcessCommandLine contains "command")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full command line, URL-decode the authImage value, and confirm an injected YAML key after a newline. Note the user and host that ran kubectl and the target cluster/kubeconfig context. 2) Contain: on the targeted downstream cluster immediately delete/quarantine any kube-api-auth DaemonSet bearing a command:/args: override; rotate the cattle service account and the cluster registration token; isolate the operator workstation if the payload was applied. 3) Hunt: correlate to the inbound exploit request (UC1) and to the resulting DaemonSet create in the cluster audit log (UC3); check for outbound connections from control-plane node pods spawned by the injected command.

Unpatched Argo CD Repo-Server Flaw Could Let Attackers Take Over Kubernetes Clusters

The Hacker News
2026-07-01 11 use cases 4 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Argo CD, a widely used tool for deploying software to Kubernetes, has an unpatched flaw in its repo-server component that lets an unauthenticated attacker run code, provided they can reach the component's internal network port. Synacktiv, which found the bug, says it can lead to a full cluster takeover. There is no fix and no CVE. The firm says it reported the flaw to Argo CD's maintainers in

Argo CD repo-server exploit: kustomize --helm-command points to non-helm script AIExploitation High
Hunts the Synacktiv unauthenticated RCE against Argo CD repo-server, where an attacker sets kustomize's --helm-command to an attacker-supplied script (pulled from a rogue Git repo) instead of the helm binary. Fires when a kustomize process runs with --helm-command whose target does not resolve to helm. Rationale: Uses the article's exact exploit primitive — kustomize's --helm-command re-pointed away from the helm binary. Cross-checked with Synacktiv reporting relayed via The Hacker News; legitimate kustomize-with-helm always calls a path ending in 'helm', so a non-helm target is high fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html • https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/kustomize/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate custom kustomize helm plugin wrapper script that ends in something other than 'helm' (e.g. a vendored 'helm-wrapper.sh')
  • In-house CI that shims helm via a shell script for private OCI auth
  • Config Management Plugin (CMP) that legitimately templates via a custom binary
  • Debugging/troubleshooting by a platform engineer manually running kustomize with a custom helm path
Suppression filter
| where HelmCmd !in~ ("/custom/bin/helm-wrapper.sh") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("argocd-repo-server","kustomize")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full ProcessCommandLine and the value of --helm-command; confirm whether the target is an approved helm binary path or an unexpected script/temp path. Identify the host — it should be an argocd-repo-server pod/node. 2) Contain: cordon the node, kill the repo-server pod, and apply the Argo CD network policies (networkPolicy.create=true) so only Argo CD components can reach repo-server (TCP 8081) and Redis (6379). Rotate the Redis password. 3) Hunt: review DeviceNetworkEvents from repo-server for egress to attacker Git/registry, check Redis 'mfst' cache integrity, and audit recently synced Applications for attacker-supplied workloads.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--helm-command"
| extend HelmCmd = extract(@"--helm-command[=\s]+([^\s]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(HelmCmd)
| where HelmCmd !endswith "helm" and HelmCmd !endswith "helm.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, HelmCmd, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "--helm-command"
| extend HelmCmd = extract(@"--helm-command[=\s]+([^\s]+)", 1, TargetProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(HelmCmd) and HelmCmd !endswith "helm"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, HelmCmd, TargetProcessCommandLine

Argo CD repo-server / kustomize spawning shell or network tooling AIExploitation High
Detects code execution on the Argo CD repo-server: the parent process argocd-repo-server or kustomize spawning an interactive shell or network utility (sh, bash, curl, wget, nc, python). This is the observable outcome of the --helm-command RCE where an attacker-controlled script runs in place of helm. Rationale: The repo-server normally only execs git, helm, kustomize and gpg; a shell or curl/wget/nc child is the direct execution artifact of the article's script-injection RCE. Parent-child pairing keeps this far tighter than a bare LOLBin hunt. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html • https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/security/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Config Management Plugins that legitimately shell out to curl/python for private repo auth
  • Init scripts or entrypoint wrappers baked into a custom repo-server image
  • Helm hooks or pre-render scripts that fetch dependency charts via curl/wget
  • Platform-engineer debugging inside the repo-server pod via kubectl exec (would show sh/bash)
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "registry-1.docker.io")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the child ProcessCommandLine and grandparent chain; confirm it is not a known CMP or debugging session (correlate with kubectl exec / DeviceLogonEvents). 2) Contain: kill the repo-server pod, enable Argo CD network policies, and block the repo-server pod's egress to any non-Git/non-Redis destination. 3) Hunt: pivot to the destination IP/URL of any curl/wget, check for a subsequent Redis connection and cache 'mfst' modification, and review new Applications synced after the event.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("argocd-repo-server","kustomize")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","python","python3","nc","ncat","busybox")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("argocd-repo-server","kustomize")
| where TargetProcessName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","curl","wget","python","python3","nc","ncat","busybox")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine

Argo CD service account deploys privileged / host-escape workload AIInstallation High
Detects the cluster-takeover payload: after poisoning the Argo CD Redis cache, the Argo CD service account syncs a workload whose pod spec requests privileged mode, hostPID/hostNetwork/hostIPC, or a hostPath mount of the Docker/container socket. Targets the Kubernetes API audit trail of the malicious manifest being applied. Rationale: Ties the article's outcome ('Argo CD deployed an attacker-supplied workload') to the concrete host-escape primitives (privileged, hostPID, docker.sock) that a takeover payload needs, scoped to the Argo CD service account as the requestor so normal privileged system pods don't match. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html • https://cycode.com/blog/revealing-argo-cd-critical-vulnerability/
ATT&CKT1610 T1072
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate privileged DaemonSets (CNI, CSI, node-exporter, Falco) that Argo CD genuinely manages via GitOps
  • A platform team intentionally deploying a privileged monitoring agent through Argo CD
  • hostNetwork ingress controllers deployed by Argo CD
  • Cluster bootstrap/app-of-apps sync that includes system components with hostPath mounts
Suppression filter
| where Namespace !in ("kube-system","monitoring","argocd") and not (Name has_any ("cni","csi","node-exporter","falco","ingress"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: diff the offending manifest against the Git source of truth — if the privileged spec is not in the declared repo, it is Redis cache poisoning. Confirm the source Application and repoURL. 2) Contain: pause auto-sync on the affected Application, delete the malicious workload, rotate the Redis password, and enable network policies isolating repo-server/Redis. 3) Hunt: enumerate all pods created by the argocd SA in the window, check for reverse shells / crypto miners in those pods, and validate no ClusterRoleBinding was added for the argocd SA.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend Res = tostring(ObjectRef.resource)
| where Res in ("pods","deployments","daemonsets","statefulsets","replicasets")
| extend Requestor = tostring(Username)
| where Requestor has "argocd"
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where ReqStr has_any ('"privileged":true','"hostPID":true','"hostNetwork":true','"hostIPC":true','/var/run/docker.sock','/var/run/crio/crio.sock','"hostPath"')
| project TimeGenerated, Requestor, Verb, Res, Namespace=tostring(ObjectRef.namespace), Name=tostring(ObjectRef.name), UserAgent, RequestUri

references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html
  - https://cycode.com/blog/revealing-argo-cd-critical-vulnerability/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/02
tags:
  - attack.t1610
  - attack.t1072
logsource:
  product: kubernetes
  service: audit
detection:
  selection:
    verb:
      - create
      - update
      - patch
    user.username|contains: 'argocd'
  payload:
    requestObject|contains:
      - '"privileged":true'
      - '"hostPID":true'
      - '"hostNetwork":true'
      - '/var/run/docker.sock'
  condition: selection and payload
level: high
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR update OR patch) @objectRef.resource:(pods OR deployments OR daemonsets OR statefulsets) @user.username:*argocd* (@requestObject.spec.hostPID:true OR @requestObject.spec.hostNetwork:true OR @requestObject.spec.volumes.hostPath.path:\/var\/run\/docker.sock OR @requestObject.spec.containers.securityContext.privileged:true)
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype="kube:apiserver:audit" verb IN ("create","update","patch") "objectRef.resource" IN ("pods","deployments","daemonsets","statefulsets","replicasets") "user.username"="*argocd*" | spath | search ("requestObject.spec.hostPID"=true OR "requestObject.spec.hostNetwork"=true OR "requestObject.spec.hostIPC"=true OR "requestObject.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged"=true OR "requestObject.spec.template.spec.containers{}.securityContext.privileged"=true OR "requestObject.spec.volumes{}.hostPath.path"="/var/run/docker.sock") | table _time user.username verb objectRef.namespace objectRef.name objectRef.resource
ClusterRoleBinding granting elevated rights to Argo CD service account AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects post-compromise privilege escalation where a RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding is created referencing an Argo CD service account and grants cluster-admin or wildcard verbs, consolidating the 'full cluster takeover' the article warns about. Targets the Kubernetes RBAC audit trail. Rationale: The article's stated impact is 'full cluster takeover', which requires elevated RBAC; a new binding tying the argocd SA to cluster-admin is the highest-fidelity signal of that escalation and rarely happens outside of initial install. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9766-5277-j5hr
ATT&CKT1098 T1548
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Initial Argo CD install/upgrade via Helm that legitimately binds the argocd application-controller to broad roles
  • GitOps-managed RBAC where the argocd SA role is declared in Git and reconciled
  • Platform team intentionally granting Argo CD cluster-admin for multi-cluster management
  • Disaster-recovery re-provisioning of the Argo CD namespace
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "helm" and Requestor !has "system:serviceaccount:kube-system"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify who (user.username / UserAgent) created the binding — an install via 'helm'/'argocd' user agent during a maintenance window is likely benign; an ad-hoc kubectl or the argocd SA itself creating its own escalation is not. 2) Contain: delete the offending ClusterRoleBinding, revoke/rotate the argocd SA token, and enable network policies. 3) Hunt: review all actions taken by the argocd SA after the binding, enumerate new workloads and secrets accessed, and check Redis cache integrity.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend Res = tostring(ObjectRef.resource)
| where Res in ("clusterrolebindings","rolebindings")
| extend ReqStr = tostring(RequestObject)
| where ReqStr has_any ("argocd","argo-cd")
| where ReqStr has_any ("cluster-admin","\"verbs\":[\"*\"]","\"*\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Requestor=tostring(Username), Verb, Res, Name=tostring(ObjectRef.name), UserAgent, RequestObject
title: RBAC Binding Elevates Argo CD Service Account to Cluster-Admin

source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR update OR patch) @objectRef.resource:(clusterrolebindings OR rolebindings) @requestObject.subjects.name:*argocd* @requestObject.roleRef.name:(cluster-admin OR *admin*)
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype="kube:apiserver:audit" verb IN ("create","update","patch") "objectRef.resource" IN ("clusterrolebindings","rolebindings") | spath | search ("requestObject.subjects{}.name"="*argocd*" OR "requestObject.subjects{}.name"="*argo-cd*") AND ("requestObject.roleRef.name"="cluster-admin" OR "requestObject.roleRef.name"="*admin*") | table _time user.username verb objectRef.name requestObject.roleRef.name requestObject.subjects{}.name
New Argo CD Application/ApplicationSet pointing to external Git repo AIInstallation Medium
Hunts persistence via a backdoored Argo CD Application: creation or mutation of an applications.argoproj.io / applicationsets.argoproj.io resource whose source repoURL points at an external or untrusted Git host, which would let an attacker continuously reconcile malicious manifests into the cluster. Surfaces the repoURL for analyst triage against the org allowlist. Rationale: The attack reconciles workloads from an attacker-controlled Git repo; monitoring Application/ApplicationSet CRD writes and surfacing repoURL lets analysts spot a source pointed at an untrusted host. Left as hunting because the trusted-repo allowlist is org-specific and cannot be hardcoded. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/unpatched-argo-cd-repo-server-flaw.html • https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/security/
ATT&CKT1525 T1072
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Routine GitOps onboarding of a new legitimate Application by the platform team
  • App-of-apps pattern generating many child Applications from a template
  • Developers self-servicing new Applications pointed at approved internal GitLab/GitHub Enterprise
  • Migration of Applications between repos during a repo consolidation
Response runbook
1) Triage: compare RepoURL against the approved Git host allowlist; a public/raw-IP or newly registered domain source is suspicious. Confirm who created it (Requestor/UserAgent). 2) Contain: pause auto-sync and delete the Application if the repo is untrusted; enable network policies. 3) Hunt: inspect the manifests that repo would render (privileged specs, external images), correlate with UC3/UC4, and rotate Argo CD repo credentials given CVE-2025-55190/CVE-2026-42880 secret-exposure history.
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where Verb in ("create","update","patch")
| extend Res = tostring(ObjectRef.resource)
| where Res in ("applications","applicationsets")
| extend RepoURL = tostring(RequestObject.spec.source.repoURL)
| extend RepoSources = tostring(RequestObject.spec.sources)
| extend RepoTemplate = tostring(RequestObject.spec.template.spec.source.repoURL)
| where isnotempty(RepoURL) or isnotempty(RepoSources) or isnotempty(RepoTemplate)
| project TimeGenerated, Requestor=tostring(Username), Verb, Res, AppName=tostring(ObjectRef.name), RepoURL, RepoTemplate, RepoSources, UserAgent
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:(create OR update OR patch) @objectRef.resource:(applications OR applicationsets) (@requestObject.spec.source.repoURL:* OR @requestObject.spec.template.spec.source.repoURL:*)
CLOUD
index=* sourcetype="kube:apiserver:audit" verb IN ("create","update","patch") "objectRef.resource" IN ("applications","applicationsets") | spath | eval repoURL=coalesce('requestObject.spec.source.repoURL','requestObject.spec.template.spec.source.repoURL') | where isnotnull(repoURL) | table _time user.username verb objectRef.namespace objectRef.name repoURL

Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

ImFileEvent

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)

| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-31989", "CVE-2025-55190", "CVE-2026-42880")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Suspicious MFA Bypass or MFA Reset Activity · [LLM] Credential Stuffing and Brute Force Against Enterprise Accounts · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Lateral Movement via Valid Compromised Credentials · [LLM] Reconnaissance and Information Gathering Pre-Exploitation · [LLM] Bulk data staging and exfiltration via MEGA / rclone · [LLM] Adversary lurking in incident-response chat tools and calls · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
Suspicious MFA Bypass or MFA Reset Activity AIExploitation Medium
Hunts Scattered Spider's signature MFA-fatigue / push-bombing pattern: a burst of rejected MFA challenges for a single user followed shortly by a successful sign-in, indicating the user (or a help-desk-reset factor) eventually approved an attacker-driven prompt. Article-specific because the crew's core play is talking help desks into resetting/approving logins rather than breaking software. Rationale: Uses the exact Entra/Azure AD MFA-denied result code 500121 followed by a success inside the same fatigue window — the documented Scattered Spider push-bombing + help-desk-reset signature (CISA AA23-320A). Threshold of 5 rejects/hr is above legitimate user behaviour. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-320a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/
ATT&CKT1621 T1556.006
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User genuinely mis-taps 'Deny' several times on a real prompt before approving
  • Authenticator app time-drift causing repeated failed OTP entries then a correct one
  • Shared/service account where multiple humans trigger prompts for the same identity
  • Poor cellular connectivity dropping push notifications until a retry succeeds
  • Newly enrolled device where the user fumbles first-time MFA setup
Suppression filter
| where IPAddress !in (dynamic(["<corp egress IPs are known-good; add tenant CIDRs>"])) | where Country !in ("<home country>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the AccountUpn's sign-in log around FirstDenial–SuccessTime; check the success IPAddress/Country vs the user's baseline and whether a help-desk password/MFA reset preceded it in AuditLogs. 2) Contain: if the success came from a new IP/geo or an unrecognised device, revoke sessions (Revoke-MgUserSignInSession), require password reset, and re-verify the MFA method the user actually controls. 3) Hunt: search AuditLogs for 'Update user'/'security info registered' on the same account, and pivot to any post-auth Teams/SharePoint access from the suspicious IP.
let denials = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 500121   // MFA denied / not completed = push-bombing
| summarize DenialCount = count(), FirstDenial = min(Timestamp), LastDenial = max(Timestamp) by AccountUpn, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where DenialCount >= 5;      // 5 rejected pushes/hr = fatigue attempt (P99 legit <=2)
let successes = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| project SuccessTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country;
denials
| join kind=inner successes on AccountUpn
| where SuccessTime between (FirstDenial .. LastDenial + 30m)
| project AccountUpn, FirstDenial, LastDenial, DenialCount, SuccessTime, IPAddress, Country
| order by LastDenial desc
let denials = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == "500121"   // MFA denied / not completed
| summarize DenialCount = count(), FirstDenial = min(TimeGenerated), LastDenial = max(TimeGenerated) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where DenialCount >= 5;
let successes = SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType == "0"
| project SuccessTime = TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, LocationDetails;
denials
| join kind=inner successes on UserPrincipalName
| where SuccessTime between (FirstDenial .. LastDenial + 30m)
| project UserPrincipalName, FirstDenial, LastDenial, DenialCount, SuccessTime, IPAddress, LocationDetails
| order by LastDenial desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:500121

Credential Stuffing and Brute Force Against Enterprise Accounts AIExploitation Medium
Detects password-spray / credential-stuffing bursts against Entra ID: a single source IP producing invalid-credential failures across many distinct user accounts within an hour. Grounds the article's 'hacking charges' and the group's documented large-scale credential abuse into an actionable identity detection. Rationale: Pivots on Entra failure code 50126 (bad credentials) aggregated by source IP with a distinct-user fan-out threshold — the canonical spray shape. 20 distinct victims/IP/hr is well above any single legitimate misconfigured client. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-320a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/
ATT&CKT1110.003 T1110.004
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Misconfigured on-prem app or MFA server retrying stale creds for many mailboxes from one NAT egress
  • Corporate VPN/NAT gateway aggregating many users behind one IP after a mass password expiry
  • Legacy IMAP/POP client farm with cached bad passwords post rotation
  • Pen-test / red-team password-spray engagement
  • SSO migration causing bulk auth failures from a single connector IP
Suppression filter
| where IPAddress !in (dynamic(["<corp NAT/VPN egress CIDRs>"]))
Response runbook
1) Triage: review the source IP's ASN/geo and whether it matches a known corporate egress; list the targeted users and check if any subsequently succeeded from the same IP. 2) Contain: block the source IP at the identity provider / Conditional Access named-location, and force reset on any account that authenticated successfully from it. 3) Hunt: search for the same IP in successful sign-ins (ResultType 0) and for follow-on MFA-registration or Teams/SharePoint access from those sessions.
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ErrorCode == 50126   // invalid username or password
| summarize TargetedUsers = dcount(AccountUpn), FailedAttempts = count(), Users = make_set(AccountUpn, 50) by IPAddress, Country, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where TargetedUsers >= 20   // >=20 distinct users sprayed from one IP/hr
| order by TargetedUsers desc
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType == "50126"   // invalid username or password
| summarize TargetedUsers = dcount(UserPrincipalName), FailedAttempts = count(), Users = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 50) by IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where TargetedUsers >= 20
| order by TargetedUsers desc
source:azure.activeDirectory @evt.name:"Sign-in activity" @properties.status.errorCode:(50126 OR 50053 OR 50055)
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` dc(Authentication.user) as TargetedUsers count as FailedAttempts from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.signature_id="50126" by Authentication.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where TargetedUsers>=20 | sort - TargetedUsers
| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Authentication.user) as TargetedUsers count as FailedAttempts from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=failure Authentication.signature_id="50126" by Authentication.src _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where TargetedUsers>=20 | sort - TargetedUsers
Lateral Movement via Valid Compromised Credentials AIActions on Objectives Medium
Surfaces post-compromise use of valid credentials by flagging a single account that successfully signs in from multiple distinct IPs or countries within a short window — the impossible-travel / concurrent-session pattern Scattered Spider produces once inside. Complements the credential-access detections by catching the movement that follows a help-desk-driven reset. Rationale: Anti-baseline of successful (ResultType 0) sign-ins fanning out across IPs/countries per account per hour is the cleanest 'stolen valid credential in active use' signal; no invented columns, works on both Entra schemas. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-320a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1021.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User on corporate VPN/ZTNA that egresses through multiple regional PoPs
  • Mobile user roaming between cellular and Wi-Fi networks with different public IPs
  • Legitimate frequent traveller or a user plus their MDM-managed devices in different networks
  • Cloud/SaaS service accessing on the user's behalf from datacentre IPs
  • Household with dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 flipping public addresses
Suppression filter
| where IPs !has_any ("<corporate VPN egress CIDRs>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: map each IP to ASN/geo and device; confirm whether the geos are physically reconcilable and whether any IP is a hosting/VPN provider common to Scattered Spider. 2) Contain: revoke sessions and require re-auth with a phishing-resistant method; if a hosting-provider IP is present, block it via Conditional Access. 3) Hunt: from the suspect IP/session, pivot to DeviceLogonEvents for RDP/SSH (LogonType RemoteInteractive) into sensitive hosts and to any privileged-role assignment in AuditLogs.
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| summarize IPCount = dcount(IPAddress), CountryCount = dcount(Country), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 20), Countries = make_set(Country, 20) by AccountUpn, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where CountryCount >= 2 or IPCount >= 5   // same account, many geos/IPs within an hour
| order by IPCount desc
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ResultType == "0"
| extend Country = tostring(parse_json(tostring(LocationDetails)).countryOrRegion)
| summarize IPCount = dcount(IPAddress), CountryCount = dcount(Country), IPs = make_set(IPAddress, 20), Countries = make_set(Country, 20) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where CountryCount >= 2 or IPCount >= 5
| order by IPCount desc

| tstats summariesonly=false dc(Authentication.src) as IPCount values(Authentication.src) as IPs from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication where Authentication.action=success by Authentication.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | where IPCount>=5 | sort - IPCount
Reconnaissance and Information Gathering Pre-Exploitation AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a burst of internal directory/domain enumeration (net group, nltest, adfind, Get-AD* cmdlets) from a single interactive user account — the recon Scattered Spider runs after gaining a foothold to locate admins and sensitive shares. Hunts the specific reconnaissance tooling, not generic PowerShell use. Rationale: Ties named recon binaries (nltest, adfind) and specific Get-AD* cmdlets to a per-user hourly burst threshold, excluding machine accounts — high-signal for hands-on-keyboard enumeration rather than routine admin scripting. Cross-checked against: • https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-320a • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1015/
ATT&CKT1087.002 T1482
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin or helpdesk running net group / Get-ADGroupMember for legitimate access reviews
  • Monitoring/IAM tooling enumerating AD on a schedule under a service account
  • SCCM/Intune or vulnerability scanner performing domain discovery
  • Onboarding scripts querying groups for new-hire provisioning
  • Security team's own AD-audit tooling (e.g. PingCastle, BloodHound collector by IT)
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("<sanctioned admin/service accounts>") | where DeviceName !in~ ("<known admin jump hosts>")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the AccountName is a sanctioned admin/service identity and whether the host is an admin jump box; review the full command set for trust/DC enumeration. 2) Contain: if the account is a standard user, disable it and isolate the device pending review. 3) Hunt: pivot from the same account/host to subsequent lateral logons, credential-access tooling, and archive/exfil binaries (rclone, 7z) to place this recon in a kill chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where (FileName in~ ("net.exe","net1.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("group \"domain admins\"","group /domain","user /domain","group \"enterprise admins\""))
    or (FileName =~ "nltest.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/domain_trusts","/dclist","/trusted_domains"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Get-ADUser","Get-ADGroup","Get-ADGroupMember","Get-ADComputer","Get-ADDomainController"))
    or (FileName =~ "adfind.exe")
| summarize CmdCount = count(), Cmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 20), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where CmdCount >= 5   // burst of directory recon in one hour
| order by CmdCount desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| extend Proc = tolower(NewProcessName)
| where (Proc endswith "\\net.exe" or Proc endswith "\\net1.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("group \"domain admins\"","group /domain","user /domain")
    or Proc endswith "\\nltest.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/domain_trusts","/dclist")
    or (Proc endswith "\\powershell.exe" or Proc endswith "\\pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("Get-ADUser","Get-ADGroup","Get-ADComputer","Get-ADDomainController")
    or Proc endswith "\\adfind.exe"
| summarize CmdCount = count(), Cmds = make_set(CommandLine, 20) by Computer, SubjectUserName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where CmdCount >= 5
| order by CmdCount desc

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ImageFileName=/\\(net|net1|nltest|adfind)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(\/domain|domain admins|domain_trusts|\/dclist)/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/Get-AD(User|Group|GroupMember|Computer|DomainController)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function=count())
| _count >= 5
