| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| sort - lastTime
Cursor-spawned terminal command targets sandbox helper, dotfiles, or symlink AIInstallation Medium
Hunts shell commands launched by the Cursor agent (parent Cursor/cursorsandbox) whose command line writes to the sandbox helper directory, shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.bashrc, etc.), or creates a symlink ('ln -s'). This is the operational fingerprint of a zero-click prompt-injection turning run_terminal_cmd into a sandbox-escape/persistence write per DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548 working_directory, CVE-2026-50549 symlink fallback). Rationale: Pivots on the article's specific mechanism — Cursor's run_terminal_cmd spawning a shell that writes the sandbox helper path or shell-init files (and 'ln -s' for the CVE-2026-50549 symlink door); parent=Cursor plus sensitive-path targets keeps it article-specific rather than generic dotfile monitoring. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-cursor-flaws-could-let-prompt.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/cursor-ide-rce-vulnerabilities/
ATT&CKT1546.004 T1059.004 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer explicitly asks the Cursor agent to 'add an alias to my .zshrc' or configure their shell environment
  • Cursor running a legitimate project setup script that touches ~/.zprofile (e.g. nvm/rbenv installers)
  • Agent creating in-project symlinks for a build task with 'ln -s' that never leaves the workspace
  • Toolchain installers (Homebrew, pyenv) run via the agent appending to shell rc files
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers") or ProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the full ProcessCommandLine — is the write target inside the project or a system/home path (helper dir, ~/.zshrc)? A write to cursorsandbox or an 'ln -s' pointing outside the workspace is high-confidence malicious; an in-project alias edit is likely benign. 2) Contain: if the target is the helper or an out-of-tree symlink, isolate the host, terminate the Cursor session, and check UC1 for an actual helper overwrite. 3) Hunt: identify what the agent was reading (MCP server response / web-search result) to find the injected prompt source, and review the host for post-escape commands running outside the sandbox.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("Cursor","cursorsandbox")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","python3","perl","ruby")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers",".zshrc",".zprofile",".zshenv",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile")
    or ProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("Cursor","cursorsandbox")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("bash","zsh","sh","dash","node","python3","perl","ruby")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("cursorsandbox","/Contents/Resources/app/resources/helpers",".zshrc",".zprofile",".zshenv",".bashrc",".bash_profile",".profile")
    or TargetProcessCommandLine has "ln -s"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Cursor Agent Shell Command Targets Sandbox Helper or Shell Startup Files (DuneSlide)
id: 2a91c4de-77b6-4f18-9c3d-1e6a0b8f4c22

Vulnerable Cursor install below 3.0 exposed to DuneSlide (CVE-2026-50548/50549) AIWeaponization High
Exposure hunt that surfaces every managed endpoint running Cursor below version 3.0, the fixed release (April 2). All pre-3.0 builds are affected by both DuneSlide sandbox-escape flaws, so this drives patch prioritisation for a tool the vendor says is used by half the Fortune 500. Rationale: Uses the article's fixed-version fact (patched in Cursor 3.0, released April 2; every version before 3.0 affected) and both CVE IDs to produce a deployable exposure list rather than a behavioural alert. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-cursor-flaws-could-let-prompt.html • https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-50549
ATT&CKT1203
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A device showing 3.0.0-nightly/insiders build where the parser truncates the pre-release suffix (verify actual build)
  • Cursor forks or renamed portable copies matching 'cursor' that are not Anysphere's editor
  • Stale TVM inventory reporting a version that was already upgraded (re-scan to confirm)
  • Non-Anysphere software literally named 'Cursor' (vendor filter mitigates but verify)
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reported SoftwareVersion is genuinely below 3.0 and the vendor is Anysphere/Cursor, not a name collision; prioritise internet-facing developer laptops and users who enable MCP servers or web-search tools. 2) Contain: push Cursor 3.0+ via the software-deployment channel; where immediate patching isn't possible, advise disabling untrusted MCP servers and the agent's web-search tool to remove the prompt-injection entry point. 3) Hunt: cross-reference these hosts against UC1/UC2 file and process detections to check whether any pre-3.0 host already saw a sandbox-helper write.
DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
| where SoftwareName has "cursor"
| where SoftwareVendor has_any ("anysphere","cursor")
| extend MajorVersion = toint(extract(@"^(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion))
| where isnotempty(MajorVersion) and MajorVersion < 3
| project DeviceName, DeviceId, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, EndOfSupportStatus
| order by DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-50548","CVE-2026-50549")
    or (SoftwareName has "cursor" and toint(extract(@"^(\d+)", 1, SoftwareVersion)) < 3)
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by DeviceName asc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50548", "CVE-2026-50549")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-50548", "CVE-2026-50549")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents

| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5") or SHA1 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5") or MD5 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5") or SHA1 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5") or MD5 in~ ("07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["07c39f79ab92fb21557b82283472dce1c112f577d796111fb752c3c6d84c86b5"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026 Cybersecurity Assessment: The Gap Between Awareness and Resilience

The Hacker News
2026-07-01 7 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Organizations have never had greater awareness of cyber risk. Yet turning that awareness into operational resilience has never been more challenging. The 2026 Bitdefender Cybersecurity Assessment confirms this is the case, as this year's findings reveal a series of surprising contradictions. Here are a few examples, based on the independent survey of 1,200 IT and cybersecurity professionals

ATT&CKT1190 T1204.002 T1219 T1528 T1566

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

The SOC Files: ScreenConnect masked as freeware. An inside look at a large-scale campaign

Securelist (Kaspersky)
2026-07-01 15 use cases 11 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Kaspersky experts have uncovered a malicious network infrastructure for delivering AsyncRAT. The Trojan is dropped via compromised ScreenConnect software. In this post, we break down the infection chain and analyze the C2 infrastructure.

ATT&CKT1027 T1053.005 T1055.012 T1059.001 T1059.003 T1190 T1204.002 T1218.005 T1218.011 T1219 T1574.002
Domainsmora1987.work.gd r.servermanagemen.xyz fileget.loseyourip.com direct-download.giize.com studioobs.com
IPs162.216.241.242 198.23.185.81 2.59.134.97
MD587603ea025623b19…

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Fake OBS/DS4Windows freeware archive downloaded from typosquatted ScreenConnect-delivery infra
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] ScreenConnect service drops and executes VBS/PS loader files in C:\Users\Public · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — The SOC Files: ScreenConnect masked as freeware. An inside look at a large-scale
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] DLL side-load of install.res.1033.dll via renamed Microsoft install.exe (ScreenConnect loader) · [LLM] msiexec silently installing MSI packages renamed as .dll (vcredist_x64.dll / vcredist_x86.dll) · [LLM] ScreenConnect-spawned PowerShell adds Defender exclusions and disables UAC (Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1) · [LLM] Scheduled task MasterPackager.Updater re-launching wscript C:\Users\Public\script.vbs every 2 minutes · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · Service install for persistence — sc.exe / new service registry write · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] RegAsm.exe (hollowed) beaconing to AsyncRAT C2 / ScreenConnect infra contacts campaign IPs · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Fake OBS/DS4Windows freeware archive downloaded from typosquatted ScreenConnect-delivery infra AIDelivery High
Hunts endpoint downloads of installer archives fetched from the campaign's spoofed-software distribution domains (studioobs[.]com, fileget.loseyourip[.]com, direct-download.giize[.]com). These sites masquerade as OBS Studio, DNS Jumper, DS4Windows and Bandicam but deliver a ScreenConnect-loader ZIP. Article-specific because it anchors on the exact delivery domains and the OBS archive naming. Rationale: Anchors on the exact delivery domains (studioobs[.]com, fileget.loseyourip[.]com, direct-download.giize[.]com) and the OBS archive name from the article — these are campaign-unique and corroborated by eSentire/Microsoft write-ups of the same fake-freeware chain. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/26/poisoned-search-results-gpu-mining-cryptojacking-campaign-abusing-screenconnect-microsoft-net-utilities/
ATT&CKT1608.006 T1189 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User legitimately downloading OBS Studio from the real obsproject.com (different domain — should not match)
  • Security researcher/IR analyst intentionally retrieving the sample for analysis
  • Browser cache/temp write of an unrelated file that coincidentally contains 'obs-studio' in the name
  • Threat-intel feed sync tool writing IOC filenames to disk
Suppression filter
| where not (FileOriginUrl has "obsproject.com")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm FileOriginUrl matches the campaign domains and identify the downloading user + browser; check whether the ZIP was extracted and whether install.exe/OBS-Studio-Installer.exe executed. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, quarantine the archive and any extracted install.res.1033.dll, and block the delivery domains at the proxy/DNS. 3) HUNT: Pivot to DeviceImageLoadEvents for install.res.1033.dll sideload, DeviceProcessEvents for msiexec installing vcredist_x64.dll, and the schtasks MasterPackager.Updater task on the same host and across the fleet.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".exe"
| where FileOriginUrl has_any ("studioobs.com","fileget.loseyourip.com","direct-download.giize.com","obs-studio-windows-full")
   or FileName =~ "obs-studio-windows-x64.zip"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let bad = dynamic(["studioobs.com","fileget.loseyourip.com","direct-download.giize.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any (bad) or HttpHostName has_any (bad) or Url has "obs-studio-windows-full"
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName, DstIpAddr, FileName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Download of Fake OBS Studio Archive From ScreenConnect Delivery Infrastructure
id: 9c2b1e4a-5f7d-4a1c-b3e2-1d6f8a9c0e11
description: Detects endpoint file writes originating from the typosquatted ScreenConnect/AsyncRAT delivery domains masquerading as popular freeware.
references:
  - https://securelist.com/tr/the-soc-files-screenconnect-campaign-with-asyncrat/120472/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/01
tags:
  - attack.t1189
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_url:
    FileOriginUrl|contains:
      - 'studioobs.com'
      - 'fileget.loseyourip.com'
      - 'direct-download.giize.com'
      - 'obs-studio-windows-full'
  selection_name:
    FileName: 'obs-studio-windows-x64.zip'
  condition: selection_url or selection_name
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*obs-studio-windows-x64.zip OR *OBS-Studio-Windows-x64* OR *obs-studio-windows-full*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten | regex("(obs-studio-windows-x64\.zip|obs-studio-windows-full)", field=TargetFileName) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="obs-studio-windows-x64.zip" OR Filesystem.file_path="*obs-studio-windows-full*") OR Filesystem.file_path IN ("*studioobs.com*","*fileget.loseyourip.com*","*direct-download.giize.com*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="obs-studio-windows-x64.zip" OR Filesystem.file_path="*obs-studio-windows-full*") OR Filesystem.file_path IN ("*studioobs.com*","*fileget.loseyourip.com*","*direct-download.giize.com*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
DLL side-load of install.res.1033.dll via renamed Microsoft install.exe (ScreenConnect loader) AIInstallation High
Hunts the campaign's DLL sideloading primitive: a legitimate Microsoft-signed install.exe (MD5 87603ea025623b19954e460add532048), renamed to look like a software installer, loading the rogue install.res.1033.dll. The DLL orchestrates the silent ScreenConnect + decoy-app install. Article-specific via the exact DLL name and signed loader hash. Rationale: install.res.1033.dll is a campaign-unique DLL name and the sideloading loader (signed install.exe, MD5 87603ea0...) is a fixed IOC; corroborated by eSentire's chain analysis of the same ScreenConnect loader technique. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Microsoft installer that happens to ship a genuine localized resource DLL named install.res.1033.dll from a trusted signed path under Program Files
  • Software packaging/repackaging tool touching resource DLLs during build
  • Endpoint backup solution re-reading installer caches
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files (x86)"
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Verify the loader process path — a signed install.exe running from Downloads/Temp/a user profile is highly suspicious vs. one under Program Files; capture the DLL hash. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host, quarantine install.res.1033.dll and the renamed install.exe, kill the process tree. 3) HUNT: Look for the follow-on msiexec install of vcredist_x64.dll, the Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1 Defender-exclusion script, and RegAsm.exe beaconing to mora1987[.]work[.]gd on the same host.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "install.res.1033.dll"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          LoadedDll = FolderPath,
          Loader = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          LoaderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          LoaderCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          LoaderMD5 = InitiatingProcessMD5, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "install.res.1033.dll" or TargetFilePath endswith "install.res.1033.dll"
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileModified","FileCreated")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileMD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DLL Side-Load of install.res.1033.dll (ScreenConnect Fake-Freeware Loader)
id: 3f1a7c22-9b4e-4d0a-8c6f-2e5b1a7d9c30
description: Detects loading of the rogue install.res.1033.dll used by the ScreenConnect/AsyncRAT fake-freeware campaign to sideload into a renamed signed Microsoft install.exe.
references:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 @ImageLoaded:(*\install.res.1033.dll OR *\Install.res.1033.dll OR *\INSTALL.RES.1033.DLL)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 | regex("install\.res\.1033\.dll", field=CommandLine) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="install.exe" OR Processes.original_file_name="install.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process="*install.res.1033.dll*" OR process="*OBS-Studio-Installer*" OR process="*vcredist_x64.dll*" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="install.exe" OR Processes.original_file_name="install.exe" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process="*install.res.1033.dll*" OR process="*OBS-Studio-Installer*" OR process="*vcredist_x64.dll*" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
msiexec silently installing MSI packages renamed as .dll (vcredist_x64.dll / vcredist_x86.dll) AIInstallation High
Hunts the campaign's masquerading trick where MSI packages are renamed to .dll and installed silently by msiexec — vcredist_x64.dll is the ScreenConnect MSI, vcredist_x86.dll is the OBS decoy. The tell is `msiexec /i "...\vcredist_x64.dll" /q` installing from a .dll path. Article-specific via the renamed-package names and silent-install flag. Rationale: vcredist_x64.dll / vcredist_x86.dll being fed to msiexec /i is the article's exact masquerade (MSI renamed to .dll) — a .dll passed to msiexec /i is behaviourally anomalous and campaign-specific. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment
ATT&CKT1218.007 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A poorly-packaged third-party installer that legitimately passes a .dll transform (.mst) or oddly-named package to msiexec
  • Enterprise software-deployment tool (SCCM/Intune) invoking msiexec with non-standard package names
  • Developer testing an MSI build with a temporary .dll extension
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Windows\\ccmcache" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ccmexec.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the .dll passed to msiexec /i is actually an MSI (file magic) and note the source folder (Temp/OBS-Studio-Windows-x64\Assets\x86 is the campaign path). 2) CONTAIN: Isolate the host, stop and remove the newly-installed ScreenConnect service, quarantine the package. 3) HUNT: Enumerate installed ScreenConnect/ConnectWise services fleet-wide, check for the Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1 exclusions and MasterPackager.Updater scheduled task.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "msiexec.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/i"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("vcredist_x64.dll","vcredist_x86.dll")
| where ProcessCommandLine has ".dll"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName endswith "msiexec.exe"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/i"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vcredist_x64.dll","vcredist_x86.dll")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has ".dll"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Msiexec Silently Installing MSI Renamed as DLL (ScreenConnect Loader)

ScreenConnect-spawned PowerShell adds Defender exclusions and disables UAC (Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1) AIInstallation High
Hunts the campaign's defense-evasion setup: a PowerShell script (Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1) spawned by the ScreenConnect service that adds Defender exclusions for whole drives, C:\Users\Public and RegAsm.exe, and sets ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=0 to suppress UAC. Article-specific via the exclusion targets and the UAC registry value. Rationale: Combines campaign-unique script name Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun.ps1 with the specific evasion actions (Defender ExclusionProcess=RegAsm.exe, C:\Users\Public exclusion, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=0) — a high-fidelity behavioural cluster, not generic Add-MpPreference. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1548.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate EDR/AV migration script adding exclusions during rollout
  • Sysadmin GPO/Intune script disabling UAC prompts on kiosk/lab machines
  • Backup or dev-tooling installer excluding its own working directory from Defender
  • MSP legitimately using ConnectWise ScreenConnect for remote admin scripting
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("ccmexec.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","gpscript.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "ExclusionPath" and ProcessCommandLine !has "RegAsm.exe")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the parent is a ScreenConnect/ConnectWise process and that exclusions target RegAsm.exe / C:\Users\Public — legitimate admin exclusions rarely name RegAsm.exe. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host, remove the malicious Defender exclusions (Remove-MpPreference), restore ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=1, kill the ScreenConnect service if unauthorized. 3) HUNT: Enumerate current Defender exclusions fleet-wide for RegAsm.exe/Public entries and search for the C:\Users\Public loader files (secret_bytes.txt, cap.ps1, script.vbs).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("ScreenConnect","ConnectWiseControl")
   or ProcessCommandLine has "Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","ExclusionPath","ExclusionProcess","ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin","RegAsm.exe",@"C:\Users\Public")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Add-MpPreference","ExclusionProcess","ExclusionPath","ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin","Fj5NmEsp9EuKrun")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("RegAsm.exe","C:\\Users\\Public","ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin") or ParentProcessName has "ScreenConnect"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ScreenConnect-Spawned PowerShell Adds Defender Exclusions and Disables UAC

ScreenConnect service drops and executes VBS/PS loader files in C:\Users\Public AIExploitation High
Hunts the loader stage: the ScreenConnect service creates script.vbs, cap.ps1, secret_bytes.txt, msgbox.txt and 1.vb in C:\Users\Public and launches script.vbs/cap.ps1 (hidden window). script.vbs also kills all powershell.exe to cover tracks. Article-specific via the exact filenames and the ScreenConnect→wscript/powershell parent chain out of the Public directory. Rationale: The loader filenames (script.vbs, cap.ps1, secret_bytes.txt, installer_method3_stream.vbs) written to C:\Users\Public by a ScreenConnect/wscript parent are exact article IOCs; the Public-directory staging plus reflective-load chain is distinct from generic 'script in temp' noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/trojanized-screenconnect-installers-evolve-dropping-multiple-rats-on-a-single-machine/
ATT&CKT1059.005 T1059.001 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy line-of-business app legitimately staging scripts in C:\Users\Public
  • Admin logon/startup script writing helper VBS to the Public profile
  • Software installer using Public as a shared working directory
  • Security tooling writing named files that coincidentally overlap (rare given exact names)
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm the writing process is ScreenConnect/wscript and inspect secret_bytes.txt for the [SXX- encoded PE pattern; check whether cap.ps1 ran hidden and whether powershell.exe was mass-killed. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host, kill wscript/RegAsm, delete the C:\Users\Public loader set, and remove the ScreenConnect service. 3) HUNT: Pivot to RegAsm.exe process hollowing / C2 to mora1987[.]work[.]gd and the MasterPackager.Updater scheduled task; sweep the fleet for the same Public-directory files.
let loaderFiles = dynamic(["script.vbs","cap.ps1","secret_bytes.txt","msgbox.txt","1.vb","installer_method3_stream.vbs"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","powershell.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Users\Public" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("script.vbs","cap.ps1","secret_bytes.txt","installer_method3_stream.vbs")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FolderPath startswith @"C:\Users\Public" and FileName in~ (loaderFiles)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("ScreenConnect","ConnectWiseControl","wscript.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath )
| order by Timestamp desc
let loaderFiles = dynamic(["script.vbs","cap.ps1","secret_bytes.txt","msgbox.txt","1.vb","installer_method3_stream.vbs"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "C:\\Users\\Public" and TargetFileName in~ (loaderFiles)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("ScreenConnect","ConnectWiseControl","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ScreenConnect Loader Files Created in C:\Users\Public

Scheduled task MasterPackager.Updater re-launching wscript C:\Users\Public\script.vbs every 2 minutes AIInstallation High
Hunts the campaign's persistence: a schtasks-created task named MasterPackager.Updater running wscript.exe against C:\Users\Public\script.vbs on a 2-minute recurrence (/SC MINUTE /MO 2). Article-specific via the exact task name, target script path, and aggressive recurrence. Rationale: Task name MasterPackager.Updater plus the wscript C:\Users\Public\script.vbs target and /SC MINUTE /MO 2 recurrence are verbatim from the article — the exact task name makes this near-zero-FP. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment
ATT&CKT1053.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate app named 'MasterPackager' installing its own updater task (verify signed publisher path)
  • Admin creating a frequent maintenance task pointing at a Public-profile script
  • RMM tooling creating minute-cadence tasks for monitoring
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Read the task action — a 2-minute wscript task against C:\Users\Public\script.vbs is malicious regardless of the friendly name; confirm the creating user/process. 2) CONTAIN: Delete the task (schtasks /Delete /TN MasterPackager.Updater /F), isolate the host, remove the referenced loader files. 3) HUNT: Sweep the fleet for the MasterPackager.Updater task and for RegAsm.exe beaconing to mora1987[.]work[.]gd; check for the ScreenConnect service and Defender exclusions.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "MasterPackager.Updater"
   or (ProcessCommandLine has "/Create" and ProcessCommandLine has @"C:\Users\Public\script.vbs" and ProcessCommandLine has "wscript")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4698   // A scheduled task was created
| where EventData has "MasterPackager.Updater" or (EventData has "script.vbs" and EventData has "Users\\Public")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

RegAsm.exe (hollowed) beaconing to AsyncRAT C2 / ScreenConnect infra contacts campaign IPs AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 stage: RegAsm.exe — a .NET utility that should never make external network connections — reaching out to the AsyncRAT C2 domain mora1987[.]work[.]gd after process hollowing, plus ScreenConnect/loader processes contacting the campaign's fixed C2 IPs (162.216.241[.]242, 198.23.185[.]81, 2.59.134[.]97) and domains (r.servermanagemen[.]xyz). Article-specific via the concrete C2 indicators and the anomalous RegAsm egress. Rationale: mora1987[.]work[.]gd, r.servermanagemen[.]xyz and the three C2 IPs are article IOCs corroborated by Kaspersky's infrastructure clustering; RegAsm.exe making any public connection is inherently anomalous (it never networks legitimately) and is the AsyncRAT process-hollowing container from the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.esentire.com/blog/exploring-the-infection-chain-screenconnects-link-to-asyncrat-deployment • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/05/26/poisoned-search-results-gpu-mining-cryptojacking-campaign-abusing-screenconnect-microsoft-net-utilities/
ATT&CKT1055.012 T1071.001 T1219
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A rare .NET dev/build scenario where RegAsm.exe is scripted to reach a package feed (uncommon; verify path and parent)
  • Shared C2 IP later reassigned to a benign hoster (validate against current threat-intel)
  • Proxy/NAT egress attributing the connection to an unexpected source host
  • Internal vuln scanner probing the campaign IPs during authorized testing
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RegAsm.exe" and RemoteUrl has_any ("nuget.org","microsoft.com") and RemoteIP !in (c2ip))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: Confirm RegAsm.exe was spawned suspended by the loader chain (parent = script/cap.ps1 lineage) and correlate the C2 destination against threat-intel; RegAsm networking is by itself high-confidence malicious. 2) CONTAIN: Isolate host, kill RegAsm.exe, block the C2 IPs/domains at perimeter, and remove the ScreenConnect service + persistence task. 3) HUNT: Sweep DeviceNetworkEvents fleet-wide for the C2 IPs/domains and for any RegAsm.exe/AppLaunch.exe public egress; correlate to hosts with the C:\Users\Public loader set.
let c2ip = dynamic(["162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97"]);
let c2dom = dynamic(["mora1987.work.gd","r.servermanagemen.xyz"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (c2ip)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (c2dom)
   or (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RegAsm.exe" and RemoteIPType == "Public")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let c2ip = dynamic(["162.216.241.242","198.23.185.81","2.59.134.97"]);
let c2dom = dynamic(["mora1987.work.gd","r.servermanagemen.xyz"]);

| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Scheduled Task Creation with Suspicious Image / Encoded Args
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0d
status: experimental
description: |

    powershell, cmd, rundll32, encoded-base64, or user-writable paths.
references:

author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_schtasks:
        Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: '/create'
    selection_payload:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'powershell'
            - 'cmd.exe'
            - 'rundll32'
            - '-enc'
            - 'FromBase64'
